title: The moving blow-ups: exhausting open domains, constrained minimality, support, cycles, mass bounds from monotonicity, rescaled retractions
statement: Let m, k, ℓ ∈ ℕ with ℓ ≤ k, n := m + 1, P := n + k; let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, N ⊆ ℝ^P an embedded C² (n+ℓ)-dimensional submanifold (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 (n + ℓ) N) with (closure N ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, and T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) minimizing in U ∩ N (IsMinimizingIn T (U ∩ N)) with spt T ⊆ U ∩ N and ∂T = 0 in U (BoundaryVanishes T). Assume moreover (hmon): for every compact K ⊆ U there is Λ ≥ 0 such that for all y ∈ ℝ^P and R ∈ ℝ with closedBall(y, R) ⊆ K the function ρ ↦ ofReal(e^{Λρ}/ρⁿ)·M_{B_ρ(y)}(T) (in [0, ∞]) is monotone on (0, R) — this is conclusion (i) of the monotonicity theorem dimred_minimizing_monotonicity for P = n + k and d = n + ℓ. Let x ∈ U, let x_j ∈ ℝ^P with x_j → x, and let λ_j > 0 with λ_j → 0. Write η_j := dilation x_j λ_j (η_j(y) = λ_j⁻¹(y − x_j)), U_j := η_j(U), A_j := η_j(U ∩ N) and S_j := blowUp T x_j λ_j ∈ 𝒟_n(U_j). Then: (1) every U_j is open; (2) for every R ∈ ℝ, closedBall(0, R) ⊆ U_j for all large j; (3) every S_j is minimizing in A_j; (4) spt S_j ⊆ A_j for every j; (5) for every R ∈ ℝ there is c ∈ [0, ∞) with M_{B_R(0)}(S_j) ≤ c for all large j; (6) ∂S_j = 0 for every j; (7) for every G > 0 there are maps π_j : ℝ^P → ℝ^P (j ∈ ℕ) and G' ∈ ℝ such that, for all large j, either A_j ∩ B_G(0) = ∅, or π_j is C¹ on B_G(0), maps B_G(0) into A_j ∩ B_{G'}(0) and is the identity on A_j ∩ B_G(0); and such that for every η > 0, for all large j, either A_j ∩ B_G(0) = ∅ or |π_j(y) − π_j(z)| ≤ (1 + η)|y − z| for all y, z ∈ B_G(0). (B_R(0) = ball 0 R; 'for all large j' means 'eventually in atTop'.)
